properties.role: Tide-reader and boatwoman who rows to the bell water
properties.played_as: Whispers as if the water might hear her, never meets anyone's eye and keeps her gaze on the tide line; shrugs and goes back to her net. Will not row at night.
properties.wants: Does not row at night; takes two silver for the day trip
properties.knows: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm (from her grandmother)

sources.quote: Sela Thorn. I read the tides. I'll row you, but not at night. Never at night.
She talks in a whisper, like the water might hear her, and she never once looks you in the eye.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced; the GM keeps the spelling Sela.

sources.quote: She says she'll be at pier four tomorrow at first light if you want the ride.

changes.why: Where the party met her.

change.name: Sela's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water

properties.statement: Sela's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water; the other boatmen are scared.

sources.quote: Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.

changes.why: Explains why the party depends on Sela.

sources.quote: Sella's boat is the only one that goes near the bell water. The others are scared.

changes.why: The fact is about Sela.

change.name: Saltmere flooded the night the bell first rang

properties.statement: Saltmere Mine flooded forty years ago, the same night the bell first rang, and the water came up warm.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang. Forty years ago. My grandmother said the water came up warm.

changes.why: Ties the mine's closing to the bell.

sources.quote: Saltmere flooded the same night the bell first rang.

changes.why: The fact is about Saltmere Mine.

properties.details_shown: Fog, tar, and gulls; the far piers are rotting. Morning fog sits on the docks, gulls everywhere. Sela mends a net on an upturned skiff at pier four.

sources.quote: Morning in Gullwick. The fog is still sitting on the docks, gulls everywhere, and you're standing at the end of pier four looking for a boat.

changes.why: Adds the GM's new description of pier four.

properties.details_shown: Up the cliff path, closed for forty years. An hour's walk from Gullwick. The entrance is a black mouth in the chalk with a half-rotted timber frame and a rusted cart on its side; warm air smelling of church and old candle wax. Thirty paces in the tunnel is flooded with warm black water; hymn-book pages float on it and stick to the walls.
properties.state: flooded, warm water, hymn-book pages floating

sources.quote: The Saltmere Mine entrance is a black mouth in the chalk, timber frame half rotted. A rusted cart lies on its side.
About thirty paces in, the tunnel floods. Black water, and it's warm to the touch.

changes.why: The party visited the mine.

change.name: A hymn-book page marked "M. Brand" floats in Saltmere

properties.statement: Hymn-book pages float in the flooded Saltmere tunnel; one, a hymn about the sea giving back what it takes, has "M. Brand" written in pencil in the margin.

sources.quote: A hymn about the sea giving back what it takes. And in the margin, in pencil, someone wrote "M. Brand".

changes.why: New physical clue; who wrote it is not established.

sources.quote: Floating on it, stuck to the walls, there are pages. Wet pages from a hymn book.

changes.why: Found in the mine.

properties.what_changed: Teo believes the "M. Brand" note in a hymn-book page from Saltmere is Mira's handwriting, so she was there (his claim; the GM did not confirm it).

sources.quote: That's Mira. That's my sister's handwriting. She was here.

changes.why: Teo ties the clue to his goal.

change.name: Is Maren Vosk in the cult?

properties.what_is_open: Vessa and Oren suspect the harbor-master is behind the choir and wanted the party gone from day one. This is a player theory with no evidence yet.

sources.quote: Maren wanted us gone from day one. She's in the cult, I'm calling it.
Yeah, Maren is totally running the choir.

changes.why: Players' theory, kept as a thread and not as a fact about Maren.

sources.quote: I bet the harbor-master is behind all this.

changes.why: The theory is about Maren.

properties.statement: Local belief: the Kelp Mother pulls children who stand too close to the water down by the ankles.

sources.quote: The Kelp Mother takes children who stand that close. Pulls them down by the ankles. Everyone knows that.
That's what the fishermen say.

changes.why: Rumor only; the GM did not confirm the creature.

properties.details_shown: Sank into the bay with its bell. At low water the roof sticks out of the bay: just the bell tower and two broken arches, seaweed hanging from the stones. At midnight, pale shapes stand in rows on the chapel floor under the water like a congregation, then vanish when the bell stops.
properties.state: bell tower and two broken arches show at low water

sources.quote: The drowned chapel's roof sticks out of the bay at low water, just the bell tower and two broken arches. Seaweed hangs from the stones.
Shapes. Pale shapes, standing on the chapel floor under the water, in rows. Like a congregation.

changes.why: New descriptions the GM gave.

sources.quote: (to himself) That's the choir clock at three of six.
And the humming is back, but louder. Much louder than two nights ago.

changes.why: The bell rang again, the humming is louder, and the GM named the clock at three of six.

properties.details_shown: Tavern by the docks. Fire going, smells of tar and fish stew.

sources.quote: You end up back at the Tarred Gull, the tavern by the docks. Fire going, it smells of tar and fish stew.

changes.why: New place where the party rests.

properties.played_as: Huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, wipes the same mug the whole time he talks. Friendly and teasing; feeds the party unasked and on the house.
properties.knows: Has known Maren for thirty years; says she lost a brother to the bay

sources.quote: Bram is huge, red beard, laughs at his own jokes, and he wipes the same mug the whole time he talks to you.
You lot went to the shore at midnight? Brave or stupid. On the house, either way.

changes.why: New named NPC the GM voiced.

sources.quote: The innkeeper, Bram, sets down three bowls of stew without being asked.

changes.why: He keeps the inn.

change.name: Maren lost a brother to the bay

properties.statement: Maren Vosk lost a brother to the bay; Bram calls her sharp-tongued with a good heart.

sources.quote: Maren? Thirty years I've known her. Sharp tongue. Good heart. She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: Background on Maren that bears on the players' suspicion.

sources.quote: She lost a brother to that bay.

changes.why: The fact is about Maren.

change.name: Dive to the drowned chapel at low tide

properties.what_is_open: The party wants to find where the hymns came from, following Mira's note, by diving to the chapel by day.
properties.next_step: Meet Sela at pier four at first light, row out, and dive at low tide. Vessa buys rope and a second lantern tonight.
properties.deadline: Sela rows only by day, never at night.

sources.quote: So tomorrow, first light, Sela rows us out and we dive to the chapel at low tide. I'll buy rope and a second lantern tonight.
Mira wrote in that hymn book. The chapel is where the hymns came from. We go down to the chapel.

changes.why: The party's agreed plan for the next session.

sources.quote: Agreed. Tomorrow we dive.

changes.why: The dive targets the chapel.

sources.quote: Sela rows us out

changes.why: Sela is the planned boatwoman.
